question: The SI unit of 'magnetic flux' is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Weber.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Weber (Wb)** is the **SI unit of magnetic flux**, quantifying the total magnetic field that passes through a specified area.
 
• One Weber is defined as the magnetic flux that induces an electromotive force (EMF) of one volt when the flux is reduced to zero in one second.
 
• Magnetic flux (Φ) can be calculated using the formula** Φ = B × A × cos(θ)**, where B is the magnetic field strength, A is the area through which the field lines pass, and θ is the angle between the magnetic field lines and the normal to the surface.
 
• The concept of magnetic flux is essential in** electrical engineering, particularly in the functioning of transformers, electric generators, and inductors.**
 
• The unit is named after** Wilhelm Eduard Weber**, a prominent physicist who made significant contributions to the study of electromagnetism in the 19th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pascal (Pa):-**

 
 
• The SI unit of **pressure,** defined as **one newton per square meter.** It is not related to magnetic flux but is essential in fluid mechanics and engineering.
 
 
 
• **Farad (F):-**
 
 
• The SI unit of **capacitance**, measuring a capacitor's ability to store electrical charge. It’s important in circuits but does not measure magnetic phenomena.
 
 
 
• **Henry (H):-**
 
 
• The SI unit of** inductance,** indicates how effectively a coil can induce voltage when the current changes. While related to magnetic fields, it is distinct from magnetic flux.
 
 
 
• **Link to Faraday’s Law:-**
 
 
• The concept of magnetic flux is integral to **Faraday’s Law of Electromagnetic Induction**, which states that a change in magnetic flux through a circuit induces an EMF.
